subject: MerchantLabs: Canary slowdown — completion spillover & concurrency cap interaction
messages:
From: Sarah Parker <sarah.parker@merchantlabs.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ops@merchantlabs.com
Cc: tom.liu@merchantlabs.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MerchantLabs canary — sporadic completion hang and throughput drop

Morning Grace / Redwood ops,

We started seeing a canary run for our checkout flow fail intermittently this morning around 07:45 PT. Symptoms: p99 completions spike to 22s, occasional 500s for the canary, and overall throughput for the canary pool dropped ~40% for two 10-15 minute windows. Attached is a quick p99 snapshot and a CSV of aggregate metrics.

This is currently affecting our canary only (we haven't rolled to prod) but it looks like queued completions are building and not being drained; our engineers observed what looks like backpressure interacting with a concurrency cap on your side. We need immediate help diagnosing whether this is a request pileup, a model variant issue, or a serving-runtime throttle.

Can we get a bridge within 30 minutes? If there's a short-term mitigation (route canary to a fallback variant / temporarily raise concurrency cap / reduce batching) please advise — we need to unblock validation and the planned rollout tomorrow.

Attachments: [attachment: p99_snapshot.png (image)] [attachment: canary_metrics.csv (csv)]

Thanks,
Sarah Parker
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
MerchantLabs
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Parker <sarah.parker@merchantlabs.com>, ops@merchantlabs.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: MerchantLabs canary — sporadic completion hang and throughput drop

Sarah — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments. We're pulling telemetry now. Quick read: the snapshots line up with a short series of queued requests hitting a concurrency cap and then a drift in batch sizes leading to KV cache churn.

Immediate steps we will try in parallel (we can run these in < 15 minutes):
- Temporarily route canary traffic to a fallback model variant with smaller memory footprint (non-quantized variant) to see if completions clear.
- Increase the concurrency cap for the canary tenant by 20% for 30 minutes as a controlled test.
- Reduce batch target size by 25% on the canary pool to avoid large per-request latencies.

Marcus and Karthik are leading the mitigation. I'll join the bridge once it's up. Please include any stack traces or request-ids from the failed runs (if you have request_traces.zip attach).

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.parker@merchantlabs.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:05:37 -0700
Subject: Re: MerchantLabs canary — sporadic completion hang and throughput drop

On initial glance at the traces Sarah sent:
- Several requests show long queuing while worker slots are occupied by a handful of high-seq-length completions (seq > 1024). These long jobs appear to block the queue because batching attempts to aggregate variable-length requests.
- KV cache miss rate spikes coincide with the p99 spikes — likely cache churn on that canary pool.

Snippet from trace (redacted request ids):
  req-99812: queued 780ms -> start -> 18.6s completion (seq 1100)
  req-99815: queued 1.2s -> start -> 20.9s completion (seq 1150)
  req-99819: queued 90ms -> start -> 0.9s completion (seq 120)

Recommended short-term mitigations (ordered):
1) Force route to fallback variant (lower sequence-length cost) — fastest unblock.
2) Reduce batch target size and enable fast-path for small seq (<256) requests.
3) If still seeing queuing, temporarily bump concurrency cap for the canary pool by +20–30% (note: will increase GPU utilization).

I'll prepare a short playbook and push request_traces.zip to the shared drive. Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.parker@merchantlabs.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:22:14 -0700
Subject: Re: MerchantLabs canary — sporadic completion hang and throughput drop

Grace / Marcus — putting the ops steps here so we have a single runbook to follow on the bridge:
1) On the canary routing policy, set model_variant=fallback-canary and drain for 2 minutes (route new sessions only).
2) Set batch_target_size to 0.75x for the canary pool and enable heuristic small-seq fast-path.
3) Increase concurrency_cap for tenant MerchantLabs_canary from 250 -> 325 (temporary, for 30 minutes) via admin-console or infra-api (auth required).
4) Monitor p50/p95/p99 and queue_length every 30s. If p99 remains >10s after 10 minutes, rollback concurrency cap and revert routing (we prefer fallback variant over cap increase if cache thrash continues).

Note on trade-offs: raising the cap will reduce queuing but may push GPU utilization higher and increase tail due to more parallel long jobs. The safest rapid unblock is routing to the fallback variant + batching reduction.

Attaching request_traces.zip (contains redacted traces) to the drive link.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

Tom / Sarah — executive summary below that you can forward verbatim.

Executive summary (two lines):
MerchantLabs canary experienced intermittent long-tail completion hang driven by batching + KV cache churn interacting with a per-tenant concurrency cap; immediate mitigation is routing the canary to a fallback model variant and reducing batch sizes, which should restore throughput within minutes. If necessary, a temporary concurrency cap increase (+20–30%) is available as a controlled test but carries higher GPU utilization and potential longer tails for high-seq requests.

Action items (owners):
- Route canary to fallback variant (Marcus) — DONE during the bridge, verified cleared queue.
- Reduce batch target size to 0.75x (Karthik) — monitoring.
- Short controlled concurrency cap increase (Grace/Karthik) — complete for 30m window; revert on regression.
- Post-mortem to include workload-level sequencing distribution and a recommendation for adaptive batch steering (Marcus) — due 2027-05-20.

We're keeping the bridge open for two hours and will send a concise post-mortem when we have the telemetry correlated. I've uploaded traces and the canary metrics to the shared drive and created SUP-8123 in our tracker.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
